overview: Sundari is a domed capital on Mandalore, documented across Clone Wars · Mandalorian · Ahsoka. Sundari is Mandalore's domed capital balancing pacifist New Mandalorian ideals against Death Watch insurgency and Maul's Shadow Collective coup.
history:
Sundari began as a domed capital anchor on Mandalore, positioned where water, ore, hyperspace lanes, or sacred geography forced travelers to stop. Sundari grew where Mandalore's resources—water, ore, kyber, or trade lanes—forced travelers to stop, creating a domed capital that outlasted first founders. Early survey maps from the Old Republic era list Sundari as a mandatory customs point for sector governors and Jedi exploration teams. Films, Clone Wars, Rebels, Mandalorian, Ahsoka, KOTOR, KOTOR II, TOR, and Sith Empire narratives all treat Sundari as more than scenery—it is a decision point.

Ancient and pre-Republic layers beneath Sundari include buried fortresses, Rakatan relics, and Sith ward-stones that still disrupt modern sensors. Pre-Republic and Sith-era layers beneath Sundari include ward-stones, Rakatan markers, and Massassi masonry that modern engineers still discover during repaving. High Republic pathfinders logged Sundari as a waypoint during the Great Hyperspace Rush, leaving beacon towers that later wars repurposed as artillery spotters. Local archives recovered from Mandalore suggest Sundari once governed trade policy for entire subsectors before centralization on Coruscant.

In the modern era, Sundari expanded through prefab districts, orbital elevators, and refugee camps that fused multiple species into a single urban rhythm. Clone Wars, Imperial occupation, and New Republic rebuilding each added districts to Sundari; Mandalorian and Ahsoka-era storylines treat it as a live operational hub. Mandalorian-era bounties and Ahsoka-era investigations repeatedly lead back to Sundari because its ports lack the scrutiny of Core World bureaucracy. New Republic planners studied Sundari as a template for rebuilding settlements after the Imperial collapse, citing both its failures and its innovations.

Sundari has been invaded, liberated, blockaded, and rebuilt more times than most planetary capitals, making its streets a palimpsest of battle damage. Battle dossiers from KOTOR sieges, TOR planetary incursions, and Galactic Civil War raids mark Sundari as strategically contested on Mandalore. Clone Wars dossiers mark Sundari as strategically vital; Imperial Era governors exploited that same geography to punish rebellious populations. KOTOR-era records and TOR-era campaign logs show earlier iterations of the same struggle—control of Sundari meant control of Mandalore.
significance:
The economy of Sundari runs on layered industries: docking fees, black-market mediation, sacred tourism, factory output, or casino finance depending on the era. Sundari's economy mixes legal trade with shadow finance—dock fees, kolto or tibanna exports, scavenging, or casino revenue depending on era and governor. Trade guilds from the Techno Union to the Mining Guild filed competing claims on Sundari infrastructure during the late Republic. Post-war reconstruction funds often bypass Sundari officially while flowing through its shadow banks—an open secret among Bothan analysts.

Cultural life in Sundari mixes planetary tradition with imported habits from every species that ever missed a connection and stayed. Markets, cantinas, and temples in Sundari blend Mandalore native ritual with offworld imports, producing music and cuisine that signal rebel safe houses to trained eyes. Music, food, and festival calendars in Sundari are used by rebels to signal safe houses and by Imperials to track dissident networks. Jedi historians note that some of the galaxy's quietest acts of mercy—evacuations, forged transit papers, hidden healers—were organized in Sundari back alleys.

Sundari influences galactic history disproportionately because leaders, smugglers, and prophets treat it as neutral ground until it suddenly is not. Treaties, betrayals, and superweapon strikes linked to Sundari altered fleet movements across the Old Republic through Sequel Era conflicts. Scenes set in Sundari across the saga often mark turning points: treaties signed, betrayals exposed, or the first shot of a regional war. Settlement planners across the Rim still cite Sundari when arguing for open ports versus fortified capitals—a debate renewed after every occupation.
